objective.text: Keep the previous immutable release available for rollback without claiming this also reverses database changes.

difficulty.rationale: Distinguish switching application artifacts from undoing persistent state.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: Release B has failed after a migration. Release A is still available. User writes since B went live must be retained.

stem: Before switching traffic back to A, what must the rollback decision establish?

options.text: A can operate on the current schema and data, or a separate safe compatibility repair is ready.
options.rationale: Switching code artifacts does not revert the database; compatibility must be checked without assuming new writes can be discarded.

options.text: Every migration down method should run even when A supports the current schema.
options.rationale: Automatic reversal may be unnecessary or destructive; compatibility and data retention determine the recovery action.
options.misconception: Automatic reversal may be unnecessary or destructive; compatibility and data retention determine the recovery action.

options.text: Restoring the pre-release database snapshot is always safe because it matches A.
options.rationale: That can discard the user writes the scenario explicitly requires retaining.
options.misconception: That can discard the user writes the scenario explicitly requires retaining.

options.text: The A directory exists, so its database state is necessarily still available too.
options.rationale: A retained code directory is not a snapshot of the shared database.
options.misconception: A retained code directory is not a snapshot of the shared database.
